question: For white-on-red signs, what minimum maintained retroreflectivity values and contrast criterion are shown in Table 2A-5?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 2A-5 shows that white-on-red signs must maintain a minimum retroreflectivity of W ≥ 35 and R ≥ 7 (in cd/lx/m², measured at a 0.2° observation angle and a -4.0° entrance angle), and this single set of values applies across all sheeting types. In addition, footnote 4 applies to white-on-red signs, requiring a minimum sign contrast ratio of at least 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity). Agencies are required to use an assessment or management method designed to keep sign retroreflectivity at or above these Table 2A-5 minimums. Standards (mandatory): - "Public agencies or officials having jurisdiction shall use an assessment or management method that is designed to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5." Guidance (recommended): - Except for signs identified in Paragraph 5, one or more of the methods described in "Maintaining Traffic Sign Retroreflectivity" (FHWA-SA-07-020, Revised 2013), FHWA, or a method developed based on an engineering study, should be used to maintain sign retroreflectivity at or above the minimum levels in Table 2A-5; signs identified as below the minimum levels should be replaced. Options (permitted): - Table 2A-5 values for White on Red: "W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7," with footnote 4: "Minimum sign contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 (white retroreflectivity ÷ red retroreflectivity)"; the table's minimum maintained retroreflectivity levels are in units of cd/lx/m² measured at an observation angle of 0.2° and an entrance angle of -4.0°. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2A-5, where the "White on Red" row lists "W ≥ 35; R ≥ 7" spanning all beaded and prismatic sheeting columns, with footnote reference 4 in the Additional Criteria column defining the ≥ 3:1 white-to-red contrast ratio. Citations: - Table 2A-5 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Standard §2 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Guidance §4 (p.62) - Section 2A.22 Option §3 (p.63) - Section 2A.22 Option §4 (p.63)
gold_answer: White at least 35 cd/lx/m², red at least 7 cd/lx/m², and a white-to-red contrast ratio of at least 3:1.
